Both arms completed to their summary lines with EXIT=1.

assertion_analysis.condition_to_fail: The fixture record stops reaching the scoring branch -- for example if the review-in-flight phase test at recovery_classification.py:649 began treating a complete run with no live review as something other than scoring -- leaving an empty or different classification in the list.
The same row classified without a population stops being classified scoring, which would make the second control measure a branch the read is not on.

The unhanded path stops reading the live set, for example if classify_pointer stopped calling _review_run_in_flight or recovery_review_dispatch.list_live were replaced by a cached read, which reddens the positive control.

The hand-over at recovery_watch.py:1390 or the forwarding at :1567 is dropped, so the row lists the live directory again and the count is one; logs/negative-control.log records exactly that mutation and exits 1.

findings.text: non-blocking: The test drives _watch_snapshot directly and never enters watch_ticker, _quiet_beat_snapshots or _live_project_session_counts, so deleting pointers=pointers at reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py:3180 (or :2569, :2844, :2857) leaves the suite green; the three call sites the brief exists to convert are covered by no assertion, and the durability of the change rests on the middle of the plumbing rather than on its use.

non-blocking: Under one head-revision header this log records runs 1-3 as FAILED (EXIT=1) and runs 4-6 as passed (EXIT=0) of test_repeated_crashes_reach_a_reported_limit, while manifest.md:12 states zero failures in three alone-runs at head and one in three with the head source reverted at base; the single added failure is therefore attributed to load on evidence its own log does not support, and either the test is unstable at head alone or this log spans two different trees under one header.

non-blocking: The module header line names the head worktree's recovery_watch.py while the same header's cwd and PYTHONPATH are the extracted base tree, and logs/rerun-base-crashed.log:4 names the base path correctly for the same revision, so this arm's header misstates the module it imported; the arm's behaviour is base, but a reader checking provenance is told the wrong file.
